title: The Meal Kit Math
editorialNotes: Names a real brand (HelloFresh) on slide 2 verbatim; Adi to confirm that is acceptable.
All meal-kit price, retention and 2022-study figures have no source-index entry; body copy only, never hero type.

thread.element: plate whose price tag is peeled back to reveal the grocery receipt

copy.headline: Meal kits charge you $12 per plate for $4 worth of groceries.
A HelloFresh subscription for 2 people runs $10–12 per serving.
items: The grocery cost of the same ingredients averages $28–35.

copy.headline: You're paying for portioning, packaging, and last-mile cold chain logistics.
copy.body: Every ingredient arrives in its own plastic bag. A single meal generates 4–7 individual wrappers.

copy.headline: Meal kit companies have an average customer retention of 3–4 months.
items: The model isn't designed for loyalty.
It's designed for a burst of convenience spending before you cancel.

copy.headline: The irony: meal kits were sold as reducing food waste because they pre-portion.
items: But a 2022 study found meal kit packaging waste INCREASED overall household waste by volume.
Less food waste, more everything-else waste.

copy.headline: The alternative isn't meal prepping 14 containers on Sunday.
copy.body: It's knowing what you already have and cooking one thing at a time before it expires.

copy.headline: Stop subscribing to groceries. Start seeing what you already bought.
copy.ctaLine: fond shows you everything in your kitchen — and what to cook with it. Link in bio.
